1.explanation: The ComposedModal.js file defines its own ModalFooter that receives the danger prop and unconditionally uses kind={danger ? 'tertiary' : 'secondary'} for the secondary button. That makes the cancel button appear as tertiary (grey) when danger=true, whereas the base Modal component always renders its cancel button as secondary (black) regardless of danger. Once you change that conditional to use secondary for danger (e.g. kind="secondary") the styling issue will be resolved. The accompanying test and snapshot files under ComposedModal will need updating to reflect the new default behavior, and the story file documents the current expected appearance.
1.bug_scenario: When you render a ComposedModal with the danger prop set to true, the left (cancel) button is getting rendered with kind="tertiary" (light gray) instead of kind="secondary" (black), even though the base Modal component still renders its “Cancel” button as secondary in danger mode. The two attached screenshots show the discrepancy: in the default Modal the Cancel button is black, but in the ComposedModal it’s light gray.

2.explanation: The core of the issue lives in ComposedModal.js: its ModalFooter implementation uses `kind={danger ? 'tertiary' : 'secondary'}` for the secondary (cancel) button, causing it to render as tertiary (gray) when danger=true. By contrast, Modal.js always uses a secondary kind for its cancel button, even when danger=true. To align ComposedModal with Modal, the conditional in ComposedModal.js needs to be changed so the cancel button is always secondary. Any existing tests (ComposedModal-test.js) and example stories (ComposedModal-story.js) will also need to be updated to reflect the corrected behavior.
2.bug_scenario: When you render a ComposedModal with the danger prop set to true, its cancel button (the left button in the footer) is rendered with kind="tertiary" (a gray style), whereas the standalone Modal with danger=true always renders its cancel button with kind="secondary" (black). In practice this means in the ComposedModal example the cancel button is light gray instead of the expected black—see the two screenshots showing the discrepancy.
